content:
You already know some of the dates you will preach. Launch Sunday is set. A holiday will land on a Sunday. You or a guest will be away. If those dates live only in your head, preparation gets whatever time is left.

This article is about the list. Write the dates down, protect time to prepare, tell the people who build the gathering, and revise the list when the week changes. It does not choose books, series, or topics. That choice belongs to the Senior Pastor, from convictions you have already made. Settle those convictions before you fill a year of Sundays with titles.

---

## Stay inside planning

[The Senior Pastor Role](/wiki/launch-team/leadership/senior-pastor-role) assigns the preaching calendar, themes for the ministry year, message preparation, and foundational classes to the Senior Pastor. If you are the Senior Pastor, this list is yours. If you are helping, you can hold the dates and chase what is still open. You do not pick the messages.

[Defining Your Church Values](/wiki/discovery/defining-your-church-values) treats preaching approach as a distinctive your church names for itself. Expository, topical, and narrative preaching are approaches a church may already hold. This article does not rank them, and it does not assign one of them to year one.

<Callout type="important">
This guide will not tell you what to preach. That includes whether to teach on giving, and when. A thin budget is not a sermon plan. Topic choices stay with the Senior Pastor.
</Callout>

Everyfield does not build this calendar. It does not judge calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health, and it does not certify the topics on your list.

---

## List the dates you already know

Keep one working list. Add a row only for a gathering you have already committed to hold. Do not invent extra services so the year looks full.

| Column | What you write |
| --- | --- |
| Date | The day the gathering happens |
| Kind | Public preaching, team class, or other |
| Who | The person preaching that day |
| Preparation | Days you will protect for study and writing |
| Already chosen | A text or theme only if you have already chosen it |
| Status | Set, open, or changed |

Put real dates on the list, and leave the message blank until you choose it.

- Launch Sunday, labeled public preaching, with the message still unchosen
- The regular public gathering you already plan to hold
- Holidays that change the room, the crowd, or who is in town
- Dates you will be away
- A guest who is already invited
- The three Pre-Launch Services, each labeled as a team class

A holiday row is a date, not an order to preach a particular holiday sermon. Write the date. Stop until you choose a text from convictions you already hold.

When two facts hit the same day, keep both visible. A guest invited for Easter still needs a row you can read. Mark the collision, decide who is preaching, and do not hide the conflict by deleting a fact.

---

## Block preparation before you fill every date

A title with no study time is a wish. Mark the days you will study and write before you add a text, and treat those days as taken. If a new demand lands on that block, move the demand or move the speaking date. Do not erase the study time and hope the day before will hold.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the service of the word."* — Acts 6:4 (LSB)
</Callout>

Acts 6 is the pattern for this list. The apostles named the work they would not drop. Do not treat prayer and study as scraps around a finished title board.

When someone else is preaching, ask what lead time they need and write that date on the row. Do not hand them a Sunday inside the window they named. If you have not asked, the status stays open. An open row is an honest row.

This guide will not set a required number of hours. A made-up quota would pretend to measure fitness to preach. You do need a block you can point to when the week gets loud. If you cannot point to it, you have dates, not a plan.

---

## Tell the people who build the day

The [Worship Leader](/wiki/launch-team/leadership/worship-leader-role) plans songs, flow, and the rest of the service with you. Share dates on the rhythm you already use together. Share a text or theme only after you have chosen it. Do not send a year of topics so the service plan has something to hang on.

The Launch Coordinator can carry dates on the project timeline and remind people of deadlines. That role tracks when. It does not choose what is preached.

If a date changes the work for children's ministry, facilities, or the welcome team, tell that leader the practical change. A guest, a shorter gathering, or a holiday crowd is a logistics fact. Say that. Do not invent a theme so the note has a subject line.

If dates go on a shared calendar, assume a shared link can travel farther than you meant. Keep unfinished notes and private pastoral details off that public view. Name one person who updates the working copy, or you will soon have two lists.

---

## Keep team classes off the public list

[Pre-Launch Services](/wiki/pre-launch/pre-launch-services) are for the Launch Team, not for guests. In those services the Senior Pastor typically teaches Peak Performance I, II, and III. [Peak Performance](/wiki/training/peak-performance-training-series) is the membership class. It walks the team through vision, beliefs, and commitment. It is not the public sermon series, and it is not the Launch Sunday message.

Give each session its own row, with the kind set to team class. A class still needs preparation time on that row. Do not copy those titles onto the public list to fill the first Sundays after launch.

After launch, Peak Performance remains the path for new members. Schedule those sessions as classes. They do not stand in for the public text you have chosen for the congregation.

<Callout type="warning">
An empty public date is not a slot for a class title, a borrowed series, or a giving message prompted by the budget. Leave it open, or fill it from a text you have already decided to preach.
</Callout>

[Principles of Financial Accountability](/wiki/administrative/financial/principles-of-financial-accountability) keeps the Senior Pastor away from the money and from individual giving records, so messages are not shaped by donors or by the budget. Do not add a giving month because money is tight in year one. Whether you teach on giving, and when, is a pastoral call made apart from this list.

---

## Change the plan when the week changes

People get sick. A funeral arrives. The facility date falls through. A speaker cancels. Revise the list. It is not a promise that every title will be preached on the day you first wrote it down.

When a row breaks, fix the mechanics before you reach for a new topic.

- [ ] Mark the row as changed.
- [ ] Name who will preach, or mark the date open.
- [ ] Check that preparation time still exists for the person now preaching.
- [ ] Tell the Worship Leader, and any other leader who built the day around the old plan.
- [ ] Leave the text blank if you have not chosen a replacement.

Then stop. Do not fill the hole with a series a friend used, or with a subject from a budget talk that week. This article does not make topic decisions. An open date is better than a title you did not choose and cannot prepare.

If the change is only logistics, say so. A moved start time is not a new series. Tell the people who set up the room, and leave a chosen text alone.

---

## Walk the list on a set rhythm

Pick a check you will actually keep. The same weekday each month is enough, or the planning conversation you already have with your Worship Leader. Open the one working copy. Ignore the slide and the old email that still show last month's dates.

- [ ] Every gathering you expect has a date and a kind.
- [ ] Preparation time is still listed for each person who is preaching.
- [ ] Guests have their dates, and the lead time they asked for is still intact.
- [ ] The Worship Leader has the dates, and the text only where you have chosen it.
- [ ] Team classes are not sitting on the public preaching list.
- [ ] Open dates are still open.
- [ ] People who needed last month's changes have heard them.

<Callout type="tip">
Keep one working copy. A second list in a slide or a chat thread will drift, and someone will plan the gathering from the old one.
</Callout>

If the check shows a year of titles and no study days, delete the titles you have not really chosen and put the study days back. A shorter list you can prepare is the plan. A full list you cannot prepare is a poster.

On that same pass, clear any title the Senior Pastor never chose. The calendar can hold a date with an empty message. It should not hold a message nobody chose.
